items.text: AMEND AND RECOMMIT TO HIGHER EDUCATION
COMMITTEE DISCHARGED AND COMMITTED TO RULES

items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6042

SPONSOR: MAY
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the education law, in relation to certain increases in
non-resident undergraduate rates of tuition for the state university of
New York college of environmental science and forestry

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

This legislation authorizes the State University of New York College of
Environmental Science and Forestry ("SUNY ESF") to increase tuition
rates for non-resident undergraduate students by 10% per year for the
next 5 years.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1: Adds new subparagraph (4-a) to paragraph (h) subdivision 2 of
section 355 of the education law authorizing SUNY ESF to increase
tuition for non-resident undergraduate students by 10% per year for the
academic years 2020-2021 through 2024-25.

Section 2: Establishes the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

This legislation is submitted at the request of SUNY ESF to allow it to
charge non-resident students a tuition rate that is in line with tuition
rates charged at the SUNY University Centers (Albany, Binghamton,
Buffalo and Stony Brook). The increases will provide SUNY ESF with need-
ed revenue to support its academic programming. Similar authorizations
were granted for the SUNY University Centers which admit similar levels
of non-resident undergraduates. This legislation is supported by SUNY.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

SUNY ESF estimates the increase will raise $7 million per year over the
next 5 years.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
Immediately
